assertion: Overdose deaths rose in 430 U.S. counties over the past year even as the national toll fell about 12% to nearly 68,000
warehouse_value: National: 68,080 predicted vs 77,306 (-11.9%); counties: 233 rose, 593 fell, 352 equal among 1,178 determinable
sql: select sum(case when b.c>a.c then 1 else 0 end) from county a join county b (Mar 2025 vs Mar 2026, non-null)
reason: National figure true; 430 county count not reproduced (233 in CDC data). Axios page returned 403.
why_not: The 12% passage in the fetched MedicalDaily pages is the article's own headline blurb, not independent evidence; the 12% is true per the warehouse and the 430 is what is unreproduced.

assertion: Deaths declined in 842 counties, comparing the 12 months ending March 2025 with the 12 months ending March 2026.
That report covered the national estimate of 67,798 deaths for the 12 months ending March 2026, a 12.3% decrease.
warehouse_value: Oct 4 vintage: reported 67,576 vs 77,064 = -12.3%; predicted 68,080 (-11.9%); 67,798 is an earlier release
sql: select year, month, predicted_value, data_value from health.cdc_state_drug_overdose_deaths where state='US' and indicator='Number of Drug Overdose Deaths'

assertion: The analysis could not determine trends in nearly half of U.S. counties because the CDC withholds exact counts when a county has one to nine deaths
warehouse_value: Suppression confirmed by footnote; 1,629 of 3,144 (52%) suppressed in Mar 2026; 1,970 of 3,148 (63%) lack a count in either window
sql: select count(*), sum(case when provisional_drug_overdose is null then 1 else 0 end) from health.cdc_county_overdose_deaths where year='2026' and month='3'

assertion: Of 42 Ohio counties with a measurable trend, deaths fell in 30, rose in nine, and stayed the same in three
sql: same county join filtered to st_abbrev='OH'

assertion: In the Cincinnati area, estimated deaths fell 30% in Butler County, from 104 to 73, and 27% in Hamilton County, from 200 to 147. Across the river in Campbell County, Kentucky, deaths rose 31%, from 13 to 17.
sql: select st_abbrev, countyname, year, provisional_drug_overdose from health.cdc_county_overdose_deaths where month='3' and year in ('2025','2026') and fips in ('39017','39061','21037')

assertion: Rio Arriba County, New Mexico, had about 173 overdose deaths per 100,000 residents, the highest calculable rate in the analysis.
warehouse_value: 69 deaths / 40,070 = 172.2 per 100,000; highest among counties with 1,000+ residents and unsuppressed counts
sql: select max(count/pop*100000) from county join acs_population 2024
